description: Crossbow killer - spends everything on one shot and takes it back off the corpse.
_source_note: Rebuilt 5 Nov 2026 from data/reference/coa/witch-hunter.json (38 real CoA Boltslinger talents, role DPS). Replaces a 23-node tree with 2 procs in it. Witch Hunter was the worst tree set in the game when measured - 86 of 92 nodes a bare number, 6 procs across four specs - which is why it was taken first of the nineteen classes left. Every CoA reference to Rage is translated to FOCUS, which is the resource this class actually has.

nodes.name: Mechanized Crossbows
nodes.description: Increases your ranged attack power by 10% of your Agility.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases your ranged attack power by 10% and the range of your ranged abilities by 5 yds.' Range means nothing in an engine with no positioning. There is no flat ranged_ap_pct key, so the 10% is expressed as the conversion this engine does support - ranged_ap is in STAT_CONVERSION_TARGETS and agility is the stat a crossbow spec stacks.

nodes.name: Rapid Reload
nodes.description: Increases your haste by 8%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases your ranged haste by 8%.' There is no separate ranged haste pool here, and haste on a turn meter means acting more often rather than drawing faster.

nodes.name: My Trusty Arbalest
nodes.description: Reduces the Focus cost of Witchbane and Shadowblast by up to 20% and increases your chance to hit by up to 4%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim but for the resource: 'Reduces the Rage cost of Witchbane and Shadowblast by -10% and increases your chance to hit by 2%.' Rage -> Focus. POSITIVE is the reduction direction for _cost_pct, which is the opposite of how CoA writes it ('-10%') and the mistake eight talents in this project have already made.

nodes.name: Heartless
nodes.description: Increases your physical critical strike damage by up to 30%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases your Physical ranged critical damage by 15%.' crit_damage_physical is a FRACTION, unlike the crit CHANCE keys beside it which are percents.

nodes.name: Arbalist
nodes.description: Increases your attack power by 100% of your Intellect.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Level 30 Passive. Increases your attack power by 100% of your Intellect.' A live conversion - attack_power is in STAT_CONVERSION_TARGETS, intellect in STAT_CONVERSION_SOURCES - and a genuinely odd one, which is the point: it is what makes a Witch Hunter want Intellect on a physical kit.

nodes.name: Bane of Witches
nodes.description: Heartseeking Bolt leaves you dealing 10% more damage for 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Casting Heartseeking Bolt now increases your Physical damage dealt by 10% for 8 sec.' 8 sec is 3 turns. damage_dealt_pct is the status-effect route to a damage multiplier - all_damage is read only through get_talent_effects(), which never includes status effects - and it is school-agnostic here, so the Physical restriction is lost. Was physical_damage +2% per rank over 5 ranks, a flat 10% that was always on.

nodes.name: One Shot
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Heartseeking Bolt by 20%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim. ability_*_crit is a PERCENT. Was 4.0 per rank over 3 ranks, which is 12 against CoA's 20.

nodes.name: Crossbow Expert
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Shadowblast by 10% and Witchbane by 5%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim, and already a scalar in CoA, so it stays one.

nodes.name: Kingdom Hearts
nodes.description: Heartseeking Bolt returns 20 Focus.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Heartseeking Bolt is now guaranteed to critically strike on enemies below 20% health and it now restores 10% of your maximum mana.' Two halves, neither portable as written. No effect key reads the target's health for damage, so the conditional guarantee is dropped rather than shipped as an unconditional one. The class has no mana at all - Witch Hunter is Focus-only - so the restore becomes Focus, as a flat amount rather than a percentage because pct_max of a Focus pool is not a shape any existing node uses.

nodes.name: Neverending Pursuit
nodes.description: Critical strikes with Damnation refund 40 Focus.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim but for the resource: 'Critically striking with Damnation now refunds 40 Rage.' Rage -> Focus. This is the node the whole spec's economy turns on - Damnation is the dump, and critting it pays for the next one.

nodes.name: Strafing Shot
nodes.description: Your critical strikes splash 25% of the damage onto up to 3 nearby enemies as shadow damage.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Critical strikes with ranged abilities now spread Tormentor to a nearby enemy.' Spreading a DoT to a new target is not a payload this engine has - apply_effect lands on the trigger's target, not on a neighbour - so it is built as splash_damage, which is the closest honest reading of 'your crits hurt the things next to it'. The school is set to shadow so it matches Tormentor's flavour rather than arriving as untyped damage. Was dot_damage +3% per rank, which is not this talent.

nodes.name: Silver Bolts
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Heartseeking Bolt and Damnation by 8.1%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Damage dealt by Heartseeking Bolt and Damnation is increased by 15%, doubled against Undead or Demons or enemies affected by Shadow Trap.' The doubling is dropped: no effect key reads the target's creature type, and none reads whether it carries a specific debuff. CoA's base 15% kept rather than splitting the difference, since the condition is what the doubling was priced for.

nodes.name: Tormenting the Tormented
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Tormentor by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Level 50 Passive. Your Tormentor can now critically strike.' Whether a DoT's ticks can crit is an engine-wide rule rather than a per-character bonus, so there is nothing for a talent effect to set. Rebuilt as crit chance on the ability, which is the same intent - make Tormentor's damage swing - through a key that is live.

nodes.name: Witching Bolt
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Damnation by 15%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the critical strike chance of Damnation against Undead and Demons by 25%.' The creature-type condition has no key, so it is dropped and 25% is cut to 15% for applying always. Pairs deliberately with Neverending Pursuit at tier 1: more Damnation crits is more Focus back.

nodes.name: Enchanted Bolts
nodes.description: Increases your spell damage by 5% and your armor penetration by 10%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases your Magic damage dealt by 5% and your Armor penetration by 10%.' armor_penetration_pct takes percentage POINTS while spell_damage beside it is a fraction, which is exactly the kind of pairing that ships at 100x or 1/100th if taken on trust.

nodes.name: Arbalest Mastery
nodes.description: Each Witchbane you fire makes your damage 5% stronger for 3 turns, stacking 10 times.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Each subsequent shot of a Witchbane cast deals 15% more damage, up to a maximum of 150%.' CoA's version ramps WITHIN one cast, which this engine cannot express - an ability resolves in one step and nothing counts its individual shots. Rebuilt as a ramp ACROSS casts, which keeps the identity (Witchbane gets better the longer you fire it) and lands on the same 150% ceiling at 10 stacks. Status stat_mods multiply by stacks.

nodes.name: Relentless
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Witchbane by 10.8%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Allows Witchbane to hit an additional nearby enemy.' No key adds a target to an ability - it is enemy_aoe or it is not, and witch_hunter_witchbane is a single-target dot - so this is repriced as damage rather than authored as an aoe_damage bonus that would apply to nothing. Was aoe_damage +6% per rank, which did precisely that: Witchbane is not enemy_aoe, so it scaled other abilities entirely.

nodes.name: Resourceful Pursuit
nodes.description: Reduces the Focus cost of Tormentor and Damnation by 20%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim but for the resource: 'Reduces the Rage cost of Tormentor and Damnation by -20%.' The previous tree used the FLAT _cost keys (3 Focus), which is a different and much smaller thing on a 100-point pool.

nodes.name: Bringing the Law
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Shadowblast by 10%.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim. Shadowblast is the filler shot, so crit on it feeds Strafing Shot's splash at tier 2.

nodes.name: Slinging Bolts
nodes.description: Your ranged damage has an 8% chance to make your next hits 30% stronger for 2 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Level 40 Passive. Direct ranged damage dealt now has an 8% chance to grant you Slinging Bolts. Can only occur once every 5 sec. Slinging Bolts: Your next Damnation is usable regardless of the target's current health.' Nothing suppresses an ability's own usability gate from a buff, and Frontier's Damnation carries no health gate to lift in the first place - so the payout becomes damage. CoA's 8% kept, and its once-every-5-sec becomes icd 2.

nodes.name: Evasive
nodes.description: Twilight Frenzy leaves you taking 20% less damage for 2 turns.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Twilight Frenzy now grants you 20% reduced damage taken while active.' Built as a window off the cast, since 'while active' needs a channel and channels do not exist here. NEGATIVE reduces, and damage_taken_pct is the ONE status stat_mod the engine reads raw rather than dividing by 100 - the physical_ and magic_ variants beside it ARE divided, which is why this is -0.20 and Douse's magic_damage_taken_pct was 4.0. Authored -20.0 first, having written that sentence and then not followed it - which is 2000% damage reduction. audit_talents caught it; nothing in the game would have, since the value is perfectly valid and simply makes the Witch Hunter immortal for two turns after every Twilight Frenzy.

nodes.name: Escape Artist
nodes.description: Daring Escape resets the cooldown of Vault and returns 10 Focus.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim but for the resource: 'Your Daring Escape now resets the cooldown of Vault and generates 10 Rage.' Rage -> Focus. on_cast rather than on_damage_cast, because Daring Escape is a self buff and deals no damage - filtering a damage trigger to it would have been a proc that never fired, which is the quiet way this kind of node dies.

nodes.name: Crossbow Frenzy
nodes.description: Increases your haste by 5% and your dodge by 5%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'While Twilight Frenzy is active, your movement speed is now increased by 40%.' Movement speed does not exist and there is no 'while X is active' gate for an effect key, so nothing of this talent survives as written. Kept as the thing a spinning crossbowman should get - speed and evasion - rather than dropped, because the tier needs a plain pick among four procs.

nodes.name: Hunter's Cadence
nodes.description: Increases the damage your damage-over-time effects deal by 10%.
nodes._source: Not a CoA node by this name - it carries CoA's Rapid ('your Witchbane now deals its full damage over 1 second shorter period'), which is not buildable: Witchbane is a dot and its ticks are per-turn, so there is no sub-turn period to compress. Rebuilt as DoT damage, which is what compressing a DoT's duration actually buys you. Renamed rather than kept as 'Rapid' so the tooltip is not promising a timing change it cannot make.

nodes.name: Contract Killing
nodes.description: Increases all damage you deal by 5.1%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases damage dealt against enemies above 75% health and below 35% health by 15%.' Both windows are recipient-health conditions on DAMAGE, and the only recipient-health key in the engine is low_health_healing_pct, which is heal-side. So the condition is dropped and 15% cut to 10% for applying to everything - CoA's version misses the middle of a health bar entirely, which is most of a boss fight.

nodes.name: Heavy Crossbows
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Darkslayer by 50%, and your Heartseeking Bolt and Darkslayer have a 25% chance to strike again.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the damage of Darkslayer by 50%, but increases its cast time by 0.5 sec. Your Heartseeking Bolt and Darkslayer now have a 25% chance to strike an additional time.' Both halves built; extra_attack is the live payload for the second. NOTE THE LOST DRAWBACK: there are no cast times here, so the +0.5 sec penalty has nothing to apply to and this node is strictly better than CoA's. Flagged rather than silently pocketed - if the tier needs tuning later, this is the node that gained something in translation.

nodes.name: Dead and Gone
nodes.description: Increases the duration of Pavise by 1 turn and reduces its cooldown by 30%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Bolt and Dash now affects an additional use of a Heartseeking Bolt. Your Pavise now lasts 2 additional sec and has a -30 sec reduced cooldown.' The Bolt and Dash half needs a charge counter, which does not exist. The Pavise half ports, with the cooldown as a percentage because cooldowns are counted in turns. Positive is the reduction direction.

nodes.name: Slayer
nodes.description: Increases your critical strike chance by 3%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases critical strike chance of all party and raid members by 3%. Does not stack with similar effects. In addition, increases your critical strike chance by 3%.' The raid half has no mechanism - a talent effect applies to its own character - so the description says 'your' rather than promising the party a buff it will not get. crit_chance_physical is a PERCENT.

nodes.name: Bounty Hunter
nodes.description: Darkslayer and Witchbane mark your quarry, making your next shots 15% stronger for 3 turns, stacking twice.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Casting Darkslayer or Witchbane now applies a stack of Bounty Hunter to you for 8 sec, which can be consumed by casting Heartseeking Bolt to deal an additional Physical damage, stacking 2 times.' The build-and-spend shape is half buildable: the building is a stacking self buff, but CONSUMING it on a specific cast is not - consumes_stacks_of reads the caster's own stacks and only extends a DoT's duration, and Heartseeking Bolt is direct damage. So the stacks pay out continuously instead of in one burst, which keeps the rotation CoA is after (open with Darkslayer and Witchbane, then fire the big shot) without a tooltip promising a detonation that never comes. CoA's 2 stacks and 8 sec (3 turns) kept.
